newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end nearly flat, bargain hunting seen.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end nearly flat, bargain hunting seen.

text.p: Stocks closed almost flat on Thursday, putting an end to an eight-day falling streak, on the view that the market has bottomed out, brokers said.
"The market's free fall seems to be halted. The view that the market is near the bottom will promote bargain hunting on Friday," said Lee Ha-yong, a broker at Hyundai Securities.
The composite stock index closed 0.5 of a point higher at a provisional 757.59.
Brokers said lingering hopes of lower interest rates in November would help buoy sentiment.
Volume totalled 28.49 million shares, compared with 24.49 million on Wednesday. Gainers outpaced losers 582 to 299.
Brokers said the central Bank of Korea's plan to cut the reserve requirement ratio for banks to an averge of 5.5 percent from November 8 would lead to overall interest rate cuts.
"The index could rise to 780 next week," said Lee of Hyundai.
But investors were also concerned that huge bond issues next month could put upward pressure on rates.
A heavy overhang of margin loans and growing pessimism about a soft landing of the economy were also weighing on the market.
Brokers said outstanding loans for margin trading totalled about three trillion won, while customer deposits at brokerage houses were at around 2.7 trillion.
A batch of economic data released on Wednesday added to doubts about a "soft landing" for South Korea's economy, according to analysts.

The current account deficit expanded to $1.41 billion in September from a $753.1 million shortfall a year earlier and inventories rose by 20.4 percent year-on-year in September, this year's second-biggest growth after a 20.9 percent rise in June.
Korea Mobile Telecom lost 27,500 won to close at its limit of 435,000 due to growing competition with its rival Shinsegi Telecomm Inc over subscription fees, brokers said.

"Shinsegi's intitiative to cut fees for subscribers will likely trigger a price war in the mobile phone market. That will hurt Korea Mobile's profit margins," said Dongwon Securities broker Choo Hee-yup.
Shinsegi said on Thursday it would sharply cut fees for new subscribers effective Saturday.
